 Community Watchlist Portfolio Search stocks, sectors, indices or pages News Economy Quick read Central govt debt surges by 8% YoY in September
 Mettis Global • 13 Nov 2026, 3:54 PM PKT • 1 min read 
 ENG اردو A- A+ Add as preferred source on Google X f Central government debt reached Rs82.66 trillion in September 2026, up 7.9% from Rs76.61 trillion a year earlier, according to State Bank of Pakistan data reported by Mettis Global. Compared with August, however, the total edged down 0.3% from Rs82.91 trillion.
 Domestic obligations made up Rs57.76 trillion, including Rs47.92 trillion in long-term debt and Rs9.77 trillion in short-term debt; Naya Pakistan Certificates accounted for the remaining Rs76 billion. Long-term domestic debt rose 6.56% year on year, while short-term borrowing climbed 16.28%. External debt comprised Rs22.39 trillion in long-term loans and Rs2.51 trillion in short-term loans. Within domestic borrowing, Pakistan Investment Bonds stood at Rs33.54 trillion, down 1.26% year on year, while Market Treasury Bills reached Rs9.64 trillion, up 16.64%.
 At a glance
 Central government debt totalled Rs82.66 trillion in September 2026, rising 7.9% year on year.
 Domestic debt stood at Rs57.76 trillion, while external debt included Rs24.90 trillion in loans.
 Short-term domestic debt increased 16.28% year on year to Rs9.77 trillion.
 Why it matters
 The debt figures provide investors with an update on government borrowing and the domestic debt instruments reported by the SBP.
